prayerTemplate: I therefore call upon you to pay my client the said amount of Rs. {amount}, being the amount of the said cheque, within fifteen days of receipt of this notice. If you fail to pay the said amount within fifteen days of receipt of this notice, an offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 will be complete, and my client will initiate proceedings against you.
filingChecklist: Send the notice within 30 days of receiving the bank's return memo (Section 138, proviso (b)).
Notice sent by Registered Post AD / Speed Post AD
Copy of bank memo / return memo
Wait 15 days from receipt of notice before filing complaint
If payment is not made within 15 days of receipt of the notice, file the complaint within one month after those 15 days end (Section 142(1)(b)).

promptInstructions: Draft a Legal Notice under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
This is a mandatory demand notice before filing a criminal complaint for cheque bounce.
Clearly state ALL cheque details: cheque number, date, amount (in figures and words), drawn on which bank and branch.
State the underlying legally enforceable debt/liability for which the cheque was issued.
Mention the date the cheque was presented for encashment and the date it was dishonoured.
State the reason for dishonour only as the bank's return memo gives it. Do not add or infer any reason.
The demand for payment and the time allowed for it are added by the system. Do not write a demand in the body.
The warning of prosecution is added by the system. Do not write it in the body.

Give each date the BRIEF gives: the date of the cheque, of its presentation, of its dishonour, and the date the client received the bank's return memo. Do not say that the notice is within time and do not work out any period.
Do not state or suggest that any offence is complete when the cheque is issued, presented or dishonoured. On liability, use only the sentence given.
Use firm but professional legal language.
Do NOT generate the advocate signature block — it is added programmatically.
